QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_31

question.text: A donor - Shubham Family Trust - is the engaging party, and Antyodaya Seva Sangh is the SE being assessed under SAS 1000. Which ethical requirement is most directly implicated if the SIA team is asked to take on additional work for the SE?

answer.text: Cultural sensitivity, since the donor and SE may have different values
Independence and freedom from conflict of interest
Constructive feedback to the donor about programme design
Non-judgmental attitude toward the SE's funding model

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook p.108 describes Independence as freedom from bias and conflict of interest. Workbook p.125 ties independence to engagement acceptance and professional competence. Workbook p.126 notes that the engaging party may be the donor. Taken together, the principle directly implicated when the SIA team is asked to take on additional work for the SE being assessed is independence and freedom from conflict of interest. The Trap: Cultural sensitivity (A), constructive feedback (C), and a non-judgmental attitude (D) are CoC values but do not address the independence/conflict-of-interest exposure created by combined mandates. Note: The workbook frames independence and conflict of interest as the ethical pillars to weigh at engagement acceptance; pp.125-126 are the operative references.
